clue.text: Disconcerted cast

definitions.meaning: someone disconcerted is put off balance, upset or confused
past participle of cast: hurled or flung

explanation.definitionFit: Being upset is being knocked off balance, and a stone that is cast has been hurled; one past participle covers both.

clue.text: It's not scoffed at by the working class

definitions.text: It's not scoffed at by the working class

parts.words: It's not scoffed at by the working class
parts.note: scoffed means eaten greedily, not mocked, and the working class is a school class at its lessons who buy snacks from a school counter

explanation.surface: Something is respected, not derided, by labourers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffed' reads as mocked and 'working class' as manual labourers; really it is schoolchildren wolfing snacks bought at the British school snack shop.
explanation.definitionFit: At a British school, this is the shop selling sweets and snacks, where pupils buy what they scoff.

clue.text: Give out nothing from Radio Four twice for listeners

indicators.note: from says one piece is taken away from the word that follows

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: for listeners says the number is heard, spelt as a word that sounds the same

parts.note: two fours make eight

explanation.surface: A radio station broadcasts nothing but repeats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes O away from RADIO, leaving RADI; 'for listeners' turns eight into its sound-alike ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit heat or light in all directions is to give it out.

clue.text: Recalled how unsociable this is

definitions.meaning: taken back, as an offer or a product is
shy and reserved, keeping apart from others

explanation.surface: Someone remembers how standoffish a person was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'how' and 'this is' join the two meanings. 'Recalled' looks like remembered but means taken back.
explanation.definitionFit: Something called back has been taken back, and a reserved person keeps away from company, two senses of one participle.

clue.text: A level is, at length, suggested

definitions.meaning: the A in the British exam name A level, written out at full length
proposed or put forward, as an idea is

explanation.surface: Someone hints that a school-leaving exam is a certain standard.
explanation.walkthrough: A levels are the British exams taken at about 18; the A stands for Advanced. 'at length' means spelt out in full.
explanation.definitionFit: The A of A level abbreviates this word, and an idea put forward for discussion has been proposed, the second sense.

clue.text: Bit by bit, become absent-minded?

definitions.meaning: division by division, one section at a time
split into two words, to leave in the mind, to drift off

explanation.surface: Gradually someone becomes forgetful.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer after six letters for the second sense: to leave, but only in the mind. The question mark flags that whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Working one section at a time is going section by section, and a mind going elsewhere is a person leaving mentally.

clue.text: Not neatly set out like garden suburb

parts.note: as means like, in the same way
Kew, a London suburb famous for the Royal Botanic Gardens

explanation.surface: Something untidy is compared with a leafy residential area.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW is a district of south-west London, home of the Royal Botanic Gardens; the OCR stray apostrophe before 'neatly' is not on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crooked or awry is out of line, not neatly arranged.

clue.text: Substance giving peace of mind

definitions.meaning: the matter or material contained in something, as in a book's subject matter

explanation.surface: Some substance brings calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving' links the two senses, which are pronounced differently: stress on the first syllable for the substance, on the second for satisfaction.
explanation.definitionFit: The material inside a thing is what it holds, and satisfaction is a happy state; the same spelling covers both.

clue.text: Duke advanced at great cost

parts.note: advanced, as in ahead of time, means early

explanation.surface: A nobleman made progress, but paid heavily for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advanced' looks like a verb but is the adjective: ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying heavily for something, at a high price, is paying for it with a large sum.

clue.text: He gives a new order to halt ship in port

indicators.note: giving letters a new order rearranges them

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone orders a ship in harbour to stop again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a new order' rearranges the fourteen letters of HALT SHIP IN PORT; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A generous benefactor donates money to good causes, a man who gives.

clue.text: I despatch special in place of officer-to be

indicators.note: special suggests the letters are given a specially made new order

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A special delivery is sent in place of a trainee officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' rearranges the nine letters of I DESPATCH. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee officer is a cadet, and the post or status he holds while training is named with the suffix for a position.

clue.text: Coming from Lake Nyasa, land further north

indicators.note: Coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something comes from an African lake and heads to a country to its north.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts in the last two letters of 'Lake' and finishes in the first three of 'Nyasa'.
explanation.definitionFit: This East African country lies to the north of Lake Nyasa, so it is a land further north of it.

clue.text: Outrage leading pairs of scallywags

wordplay.reading: first pair SC, second pair AL

parts.note: the first two pairs of letters of the word scallywags, read out as one pair and the other

explanation.surface: A public outcry is caused by a couple of rogues at the head of a group.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening two pairs of letters of 'scallywags' are SC and AL; say them as 'SC and AL' and the phrase spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A disgraceful event causing public shock and indignation is an outrage.

clue.text: Rough treatment for unseasoned wood

parts.note: unseasoned timber has not been dried, so it is raw
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: Green timber gets a rough handling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word. DEAL, a common British word for softwood planks, is the wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfair handling of someone is an idiom built from the card-game sense of a bad hand dealt.

clue.text: A drummer gets nothing in return for musical performance

indicators.note: in return says the whole string of A, the salesman and nothing is read backwards

parts.note: a drummer is a travelling salesman, who drums up trade; a rep
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A percussionist receives no pay for his part in a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: A, REP and O run together as AREPO; 'in return' turns that string round. 'gets' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera is a staged drama set to music, a kind of musical performance.

clue.text: Put up memo about talkative flier

indicators.note: about says the note goes round the bird's name

parts.note: a memo is a short written note
the mina or mynah is a bird that can mimic speech

explanation.surface: A memo is posted concerning a chatty pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. The talking bird, also spelt mynah, is a crossword favourite; 'Put up' means propose, not erect.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone up for election or an award is to propose them as a candidate.

clue.text: In no state to circle like a bat

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: In says the word for circle goes inside the other letters

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state
to circle is to turn round

explanation.surface: Someone is too unwell to travel round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals the container; 'to' is a link word. 'state' gives the old abbreviation for California, not a condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats are active at night and sleep by day, so the adjective for night-active creatures fits.

clue.text: Pattern that's beautiful? I'll say!

parts.note: fair is an old word for beautiful

indicators.note: say tells us the contraction is heard as a word for an island

parts.note: I'll, the contraction of I will

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a lovely design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is a link word, and 'say' turns 'I'll' into its sound-alike ISLE. This is a multicoloured knitting pattern named after a small island in the Shetlands, north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional banded knitwear design from the Shetland island of that name is a style of patterning.

clue.text: Toast a sign of gluttony?

definitions.meaning: a cheery drinking salutation before a glass is raised
jokingly, two chins, a double chin from overeating

explanation.surface: A drinking salute marks the greedy eater.
explanation.definitionFit: The drinking salutation is an old borrowing from Chinese, and the playful second sense is a double chin from overeating.

clue.text: Pope with aspiration to become emperor

parts.note: an aspiration is a breathed sound, the letter H
Adrian was the name of six popes, including the English one, Adrian IV

explanation.surface: A pontiff with ambitions to rule an empire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspiration' means an ambition on the surface but is phonetics: the breathed sound H. 'with' and 'to become' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a Roman ruler who built the wall across northern Britain.

clue.text: Reptile and bird drawn by pen, by artist

parts.note: a pen is a female swan, and the male swan, the cob, is drawn to her
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A creature and a bird are sketched with a pen by a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like a writing tool but is the female swan, whose mate is the cob. 'and' and the second 'by' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: This hooded venomous snake is one kind of reptile.

clue.text: Not a lot of information on one bird or another

parts.note: a bit is the smallest unit of information in computing
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher has very little information on a certain species.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' links the pieces in this down clue, and 'or' links the definition: one bird gives one piece, another bird is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The marsh-dwelling heron with its booming call is a different bird again from the one in the wordplay, so it is another bird.

clue.text: The fashion trade

definitions.meaning: the accepted way, a prevailing usage
business from regular ..., as in losing a shop's patronage

explanation.surface: The clothes business is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The fashion trade' reads as one phrase, the clothing industry; split it for two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A usual practice is the accepted way of doing things, and a shop's regular patronage is its trade from customers.

clue.text: Pass through, or conquered be

parts.note: a conquered people are under their conqueror's rule
go can mean be or become, as in go quiet

explanation.surface: A survivor either comes through or is defeated.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue words 'conquered be' are a poetic word order for 'be conquered', and their pieces in the clue's order build the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To go through an experience, such as an operation or an ordeal, is to experience it and come out the other side.

clue.text: Where top players are trained? Right, this'll detect the high-fliers

parts.note: RADA, the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London, trains actors

explanation.surface: A question about training elite performers leads to a device for spotting stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'players' are actors, not sportsmen, and RADA is London's best-known drama school.
explanation.definitionFit: The system bouncing radio waves off aircraft is how planes and other high-flying objects are detected.

clue.text: A fat neighbour

parts.note: butter is a dairy fat

explanation.surface: Someone describes the overweight person next door.
explanation.definitionFit: One whose land adjoins another's, touching at a boundary, is a neighbour.

clue.text: Had essay examined

definitions.meaning: had a go: to essay is to attempt
examined in a court of law, as a case or defendant is

explanation.surface: A student's composition was assessed.
explanation.definitionFit: Making an attempt is the old meaning of essay, and a case heard in court has been judged, so both senses match.

clue.text: Rum-sounding-lot, perhaps, one maligns

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to malign someone is to slander them

explanation.surface: A rather odd-sounding group is accused of spreading lies about others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink or 'odd', but it is a small island of the Inner Hebrides off Scotland, whose people, with their surrounding sounds, are an example of the definition; 'perhaps' marks the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhabitants of any island, Rum among them, are known collectively by a word for island-dwellers.

clue.text: Involved in my trio, one is in this

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed together

parts.note: taken as written as part of the fodder
taken as written as part of the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone notes being one of three people in a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved' rearranges IN and MY TRIO together. The definition is cryptic: one member out of three is the smaller part of the group.
explanation.definitionFit: One out of a trio is outnumbered by the other two, so that person forms the smaller group.

clue.text: Stroke a gander

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a deflecting shot off the bat to fine leg
a quick look; to have a gander is slang for a look

explanation.surface: Someone pats a male goose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gander' looks like the goose but is British slang for a look. In cricket the word is also a deft shot steering the ball past the wicketkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick peek is a fleeting look, and a cricketer's deflected shot fine on the leg side is the batting stroke.
